name: Aperture Finance arbitrary call approval drain
summary: Aperture's closed-source router executed a caller-supplied call target and calldata from its swap path without validation, so anyone could make it call ERC-20 transferFrom() or the Uniswap V3 position manager against the token and position approvals users had granted it, moving those assets to themselves.
notes: The anchor executed only 0xd83d960d, a direct deployment unchanged through the exploit. Other Aperture routers with the same call path (0xaf34783a and 0xafc9f5bd on Ethereum and Arbitrum; separate Base and BNB Chain deployments) were drained in the campaign and are not targets.
Campaign: the attacker's transactions on four chains plus every later call into these routers that pulled assets from a third party's approval, by any sender. No such pull precedes the anchor.

Stolen Uniswap V3 positions are valued at their liquidity and uncollected fees one block before the theft. Assets without a DefiLlama price are listed at $0 except Polygon SHIB, priced at the SHIB market price.
